# Sirach 13 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Sirach 13 (26 verses)
**Total Disagreements:** 16

---

## Disagreement 1 — Verse 1

**Issue:** "Proud man" vs. "arrogant person"
- EMET: "a proud man"
- LOGOS/SOPHIA: "an arrogant person"
- PNEUMA: "an arrogant person"

**Resolution:** Greek ὑπερήφανος = one who thinks highly of himself. "Arrogant" more precisely captures the active disdain. LOGOS/SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 2 — Verse 2

**Issue:** "Iron kettle" — what it "does" to the clay pot
- EMET: "This one strikes, and that one is shattered"
- LOGOS: "The kettle strikes and the pot is shattered"
- PNEUMA: "The iron strikes and the clay shatters"
- SOPHIA: "The kettle strikes and the pot shatters"

**Resolution:** All convey the same thing. LOGOS/SOPHIA identify the subject clearly while maintaining parallel structure. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 3 — Verse 3

**Issue:** Rich man's response vs. poor man's response
- EMET: "adds threats … must beg forgiveness"
- LOGOS: "adds insults … must himself offer apologies"
- PNEUMA: "adds insults to it … has to apologize"
- SOPHIA: "adds threats … must beg forgiveness"

**Resolution:** Greek ἐπιτιμᾷ can mean threatens OR rebukes/insults. LOGOS "insults" is more common interpretation. SOPHIA retained EMET's "threats" as defensible. Both valid; SOPHIA chose EMET rendering. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 4 — Verse 4

**Issue:** "Make use of you" vs. "exploit you"
- EMET: "he will make use of you"
- LOGOS: "he will exploit you"
- PNEUMA: "they'll use you"
- SOPHIA: "he will exploit you"

**Resolution:** LOGOS "exploit" captures the predatory sense implied by context. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 5 — Verse 6

**Issue:** The rich man's flattery — structure
- EMET: "he will smile at you and give you hope"
- LOGOS: "he will smile at you and raise your hopes"
- PNEUMA: "get your hopes up" / "say all the right things"
- SOPHIA: "he will smile at you and raise your hopes"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA paraphrases. LOGOS/SOPHIA close to literal. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 6 — Verse 7

**Issue:** "Until he has drained you twice or three times over"
- EMET: "until he has drained you twice or three times over"
- LOGOS: "stripped you bare… more than once or twice"
- PNEUMA: "again and again — until you have nothing left"
- SOPHIA: "until he has stripped you bare — this more than once or twice"

**Resolution:** The Greek implies stripping/draining — multiple occurrences. EMET "twice or three times" closer to literal number. LOGOS/SOPHIA reorder for flow. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 7 — Verse 8

**Issue:** Warning against what exactly
- EMET: "not to be humiliated in your moment of pleasure"
- LOGOS: "not to be humiliated by your own entertainment"
- PNEUMA: "don't make yourself look foolish chasing their invitations"
- SOPHIA: "not to be humiliated in your eagerness for his company"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA adds "chasing invitations" as interpretation. EMET "moment of pleasure" is closest to literal. SOPHIA blends with contextual explanation. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 8 — Verse 9

**Issue:** "Decline" vs. "hold back"
- EMET: "decline"
- LOGOS/SOPHIA: "hold back"
- PNEUMA: "learn to hold back"

**Resolution:** Greek ἀναχώρει means withdraw, stand back — not outright refusal. "Hold back" more accurate. LOGOS/SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 9 — Verse 11

**Issue:** "Do not trust his abundance of words" — how to phrase
- EMET: "do not trust his abundance of words"
- LOGOS: "do not trust his lengthy speeches"
- PNEUMA: "don't believe everything they say"
- SOPHIA: "do not trust his many words"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA loses the "speeches/words" specificity. EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA all close. SOPHIA's "many words" is most natural. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 10 — Verse 12

**Issue:** "Chains" — literal or metaphorical
- EMET: "he will not spare you from pain or from chains"
- LOGOS: "he will not spare you hurt or chains"
- PNEUMA: "they'll give you nothing but grief"
- SOPHIA: "he will not spare you from pain or chains"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA loses the specific "chains" image entirely. EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA preserve literal sense. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 11 — Verse 13b

**Issue:** "Wake up in your sleep" — interpretation
- EMET: "wake up in your sleep"
- LOGOS: "wake up in your sleep"
- PNEUMA: "take them to heart even in your sleep"
- SOPHIA: "wake up even in your sleep"

**Resolution:** All four handle this difficult idiom. The Greek ἐγείρου may mean "wake up!" as urgent command; "in your sleep" could be idiomatic for "at any moment." SOPHIA preserved the literal paradox. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 12 — Verse 19

**Issue:** "Pasture of the rich" vs. "feeding ground of the rich"
- EMET: "the pasture of the rich" (poor as grazing ground)
- LOGOS: "the feeding ground of the rich"
- PNEUMA: "the rich feed on the poor"
- SOPHIA: "the feeding ground of the rich"

**Resolution:** Greek νομαί = pasture/feeding ground. PNEUMA loses the predator/prey image. LOGOS/SOPHIA close. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 13 — Verse 21

**Issue:** Friends' response to the poor person's fall
- EMET: "he is pushed away even by his friends"
- LOGOS: "his friends as well push him away"
- PNEUMA: "even friends give them a shove"
- SOPHIA: "even friends push him away"

**Resolution:** All essentially agree. SOPHIA adopted with slight simplification.

---

## Disagreement 14 — Verse 22

**Issue:** Contrast of rich/poor speakers — two separate agents disagree on structure
- EMET: "he says something unseemly and men justify him… he speaks wisely and no room is made for him"
- LOGOS: "he says something improper and they excuse him… he speaks sensibly and no one takes notice"
- PNEUMA: "they say something wrong and people find reasons to excuse it… they say something wise and nobody listens"
- SOPHIA: "he says something improper and they find excuses for him… he speaks wisely and no one takes notice"

**Resolution:** LOGOS/SOPHIA "improper" more precise than "unseemly." SOPHIA harmonizes. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 15 — Verse 24

**Issue:** Is poverty inherently bad or only in the ungodly's opinion?
- EMET: "poverty is evil in the reckoning of the ungodly"
- LOGOS: "poverty is evil in the opinion of the ungodly"
- PNEUMA: "poverty is seen as something shameful in the eyes of the ungodly"
- SOPHIA: "poverty is evil in the reckoning of the ungodly"

**Resolution:** The qualifier "in the reckoning/opinion of the ungodly" is critical — Ben Sira does not endorse that poverty is evil. All agents retain it. "Reckoning" (EMET/SOPHIA) is slightly more formal than "opinion." SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 16 — Verse 26

**Issue:** "Search for wise sayings is a toilsome labor" — how to render
- EMET: "the search for wise sayings is a toilsome labor"
- LOGOS: "devising wise sayings involves wearisome effort"
- PNEUMA: "finding the right words of wisdom, though — that takes real work"
- SOPHIA: "the search for wise words is wearisome labor"

**Resolution:** Greek ἐρεύνησις σοφίας = searching out of wisdom. LOGOS "devising" shifts to composition rather than seeking. EMET/SOPHIA "search" more literal. SOPHIA adopted.
